correctness.rationale: For f(x)=x^2/2 and the exact quadratic model, the constrained minimizer is s_k=-Delta_k as long as x_k>Delta_k. The condition Delta_0<(1-q)x_0 makes the total radius mass Delta_0/(1-q) smaller than x_0, so x_k=x_0-Delta_0(1-q^k)/(1-q) stays positive and x_k-Delta_k=x_{k+1}>x_infinity. Model and objective coincide, hence every accepted ratio is rho_k=1 for every eta in (0,1). There are no unsuccessful iterations, so C.2 is vacuous; C.3 holds because Delta_{k+1}=q Delta_k with q<1<gamma_3; C.1 fails because Delta_k tends to zero while the running minimum gradient tends to x_infinity>0. An independent exact-rational replay confirms the recurrence and rho=1, while the infinite conclusion comes from the geometric sum.
